claims.text: Most of a shop's cost is shared (nodes, database server, fixed platform per cluster); cost per shop = the month's shared cost times the shop's measured share; each way of splitting is an estimate.
The fixed cost per cluster is split evenly across shops because it does not grow with use.

Usage metering in cost-per-shop.md is a model at stage-4, not code: requests per shop (counter ADR 0016 decides on) for api nodes; orders and rows by shop_id daily for database and backups; chat connections per shop (Support, ADR 0032's support-chat service) when it exists.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/cost-per-shop.md @ stage-4 lines 3, 20-28; ADR 0016 lines 40-52; ADR 0032 title

claims.text: A shop with its own database under ADR 0026 carries that database's whole cost plus its share of the rest.

Each value of a label adds time series: a shop label on a counter adds about one series per shop per combination of the other labels; on a classic histogram, per shop, one series for every bucket plus its _sum and _count series.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs, Concepts > Data model (series = metric name + label set); Metric types > Histogram (_bucket per le, _sum, _count); cost-per-shop.md lines 33-39

claims.text: Per-shop detail stays on counters, as ADR 0016 decided; the response-time histogram has no shop label.

A trace that starts in the api is kept with probability Telemetry:SampleRatio, 0.1 unless configured; a parent-based sampler makes a span with a parent follow its parent's decision, so a trace is kept or dropped whole.
claims.source_hint: DonHang.Api/Program.cs @ stage-4 lines 101-110; OpenTelemetry .NET docs, ParentBasedSampler and TraceIdRatioBasedSampler

claims.text: SLIs S1-S4 come from metrics that count every request, so they do not depend on the trace sampling ratio.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/cost-per-shop.md @ stage-4 lines 51-52; backend.l3.trace-sampling (request metrics from prometheus-net)

claims.text: Compose sets Telemetry__SampleRatio to 1.0, so the lab keeps every trace; the lab's Tempo keeps traces 24 hours (block_retention: 24h in deploy/monitoring/tempo.yml).
claims.source_hint: docs/design/cost-per-shop.md @ stage-4 lines 46, 49-50; deploy/monitoring/tempo.yml @ stage-4 (compactor.compaction.block_retention); docker-compose.yml

claims.text: The api's ConfigMap in staging and production sets OTEL_SDK_DISABLED: "true", so those environments keep no traces yet.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/cost-per-shop.md @ stage-4 lines 47-48; api ConfigMap under deploy/gitops at stage-4

claims.text: S1 (order placed without 5xx, SLO 99.5% over 28 days; assumed 50,000/day, ~1.4M in 28 days) allows ~7,000 bad requests; a quarter (slo.md's postmortem threshold) is ~1,750; at 0.1 ~175 error traces kept.

S4 (refund request answered within 2 seconds, SLO 99%; assumed ~14,000 in 28 days) allows ~140 bad requests; a quarter is ~35; at 0.1 ~3 traces remain; the doc accepts it because each request's log is still there.
Production keeps 0.1, the code's default, with no code change; keeping traces by outcome (waiting for the whole trace, then keeping every failing one) is named only as an option in words, not built.

Retention: traces and logs 7 days in production (assumed), since 24 h is too short (Friday incident, Monday investigation); metrics at least 28 days is the doc's target: staging Prometheus keeps 2d (no volume), production has no Prometheus.

Trade-off point: finer metering and more traces give fairer plan prices and faster diagnosis, but every series and span costs storage, itself a shared cost; the driver is knowing each plan's cost per shop well enough to set prices, no more.
Keeping every trace is right in the lab: a learner wants to see each request, and its traffic and 24 hours of storage are small.
claims.source_hint: cost-per-shop.md line 46 (lab keeps every trace), tempo.yml comment (enough for one lab)

claims.text: If a higher plan promised per-shop response-time figures, the team would weigh the histogram's per-shop, per-bucket series as a new trade-off point before adding the label.
A ratio-based sampler keeps traces regardless of outcome, so raising the ratio keeps more of every trace, failing or not, and storage grows with all traffic.
claims.source_hint: OpenTelemetry .NET docs, TraceIdRatioBasedSampler (decision from trace id only); OpenTelemetry spec, Sampling

claims.text: Try it: with 1,000 shops and an assumed 10-bucket histogram, a shop label adds ~1,000 counter series and ~10,000 bucket series; at ratio 0.05 a quarter-budget burn on S1 leaves ~88 traces, S4 ~2.
claims.source_hint: Arithmetic on cost-per-shop.md lines 35-39, 58-64; 10 buckets is the lesson's assumption

Lab vs production retention reason (Friday incident, Monday investigation), from the excerpt.
